hero.title: A Minecraft server that boots in <hl>5 ms.</hl>
hero.benchNote: Same world, same machine, measured from launch to "players can join".
hero.lede: Pumpkin is a Minecraft server written in Rust. No Java to install, one file to run, Java and Bedrock players on the same world.

facts.title: What Pumpkin is <hl>today</hl>

items.lead: One native executable. Nothing to install, no flags to tune, no start script.
items.rest: Drop it in a folder and run it.

items.lead: Memory at idle with a world loaded.
items.rest: Vanilla sits near 1.8 GB before anyone has joined.

items.lead: Written for parallel work from the first commit,
items.rest: not one main thread with helpers bolted on.

items.lead: Both editions join the same world.
items.rest: Built in, no proxy in front, no plugin to install.

items.lead: Write plugins in Rust, Kotlin, Python, Go, C#, C, D, Zig or TypeScript.
items.rest: One API underneath, pick the language you already know.

items.lead: The whole server, not a core with a paid tier.
items.rest: Read it, fork it, ship it.

facts.earlyBody: Pumpkin is not finished. Not every vanilla mechanic is in yet, worlds can break between versions, and config keys still move. Run it on a test server first, keep backups, and report what breaks. The docs say what works today.

checklist.title: Feature <hl>checklist</hl>
checklist.description: Pumpkin next to Vanilla, Paper and Folia, as they ship today. Marks with a dot have a note.

startup.detail: Ready before a JVM has finished warming up.

notes.1: Vanilla waits on JVM start-up and world loading.
notes.3: Often slower than Paper, there is more to initialize.

idleCpu.detail: Sits near zero when nobody is online.

memory.detail: About 100 MB with a world loaded.

parallel.detail: Parallel by design, not one main thread.

notes.0: Game logic and background tasks run across threads, not only chunk loading.
Pumpkin has its own API. Bukkit and Paper plugins can run through PatchBukkit, which is early.
notes.3: Varies. Many plugins need updates for Folia's threading.

editions.detail: Both editions on one world, no proxy.

notes.2: Through an external plugin such as Geyser.
notes.3: Through external plugins, and Folia's threading makes setup harder.

pluginLanguages.detail: Rust, Kotlin, Python, Go, C#, C, D, Zig, TypeScript.

configuration.detail: Every subsystem has its own config file.

notes.2: Only the patches are open source.
notes.3: Only the patches are open source.

tryIt.title: Try it on a spare machine.
tryIt.body: It's one file. Run it next to your current server, point a client at it, and see what works for your world before you commit.
